## The reading, taken first-hand

The card says the `.describe()` 「still says the manager column has no product write surface」. It does not. On `origin/main` the string reads:

> `manager` is resolved from the directory rather than configured here: it reads the submitter's `sys_user.manager_id` at runtime, and **that column is not a profile field an author edits**, so until an operator populates it through one of the routes `os lint` names, a manager step resolves to nobody and the request waits.

⇒ 「no product write surface」 is **gone**, replaced by a statement about the COLUMN. ⭐ And the repair is narrated in the source, in a comment sitting directly above the string:

> ⛔ It said 「that column has no product write surface」 **until the write surface landed** — the exact staleness the pointer discipline above exists to make cheap to repair, and the reason the sentence now describes the COLUMN (not a profile field an author edits) rather than the platform's inventory of writers.

**Cited cards, re-read at this act:** #17993 **closed** (it is the PR that gave the column its write surface), #17640 **closed**, #19283 **closed**. The card's own causal story is intact — only its present tense is false.

## ⭐ Why this closure is worth one paragraph rather than a silent state change

This is the shape #18376 recorded on this board: **a grep hit read as 「the defect is alive」 when it was evidence the fix had landed.** The keyword 「manager」 is all over this file — a seat that matched on it, or on the card's own phrasing, would have dispatched a dev to repair something already repaired. What refuted it was reading the surrounding text instead of matching a token, which is the standing rule 「正命中须答谁打印/执行它」 applied to a card rather than to code.

⛔ No card filed for the staleness itself: the carrier is this card, and it is closing.

⚠️ **Reversible and cheap to reverse.** If a reader finds the stale sentence surviving on any surface this seat did not read — a generated reference page, a cached doc build, a sibling carrier that reuses the approver entry — reopen this card with that reading and it is live again. ⛔ This closure asserts only what was measured: the `.describe()` in `packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts` on `origin/main` today.
